rows.headline: Seven companies paying dividends higher than their annual profits
rows.hook: High dividends masking weak company earnings

modes.bear: Paying out more than current earnings is unsustainable and often indicates a lack of growth or deteriorating financial health.
modes.bull: Companies may be returning excess cash to shareholders from accumulated reserves rather than current operational struggles.
modes.simple: Just because a company pays a high dividend doesn't mean it's profitable. Sometimes companies pay out more than they earn, which can be a red flag for your investment.

rows.summary: Companies including IL&FS Investment Managers, CyberTech Systems, and Premco Global have reported dividend payouts exceeding their FY26 net profits. Payout ratios for these firms reached as high as 1,000%, signaling that dividend yield alone is an incomplete metric for financial health. This trend highlights the risk of relying on payouts when underlying profitability is thin or declining. Retail investors should evaluate earnings sustainability alongside dividend history to avoid potential value traps.
rows.why_it_matters: High dividend payouts from low profits may signal unsustainable business models.
